newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar bursts higher in heavy turnover.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar bursts higher in heavy turnover.

text.p: Trade buying of white sugar futures drove nearby values higher on Wednesday in an unusually high volume of business.
One leading trade house was an active buyer of March/May, pushing the switch out to $1.80 after earlier commission house dealings seen at $1.50.

The surge in London was sparked by technical strength in the New York market, where the equivalent March raws contract broke through its previous high of 10.54 cents/lb and touched off fund buy stops.
"As New York has come back, London has held its ground. Premiums have widened," said one trader.
March/March was trading around $69, its approximate level for the last few sessions although sellers were waiting in the wings above the market at $70 and $71 to cap any strength, traders said.
But activity was once again centred around the approaching expiry of the spot March contract as players rolled positions forward and continued to post large volumes of against actuals trades.
With over 2,000 lots posted as against actuals trades, London has seen the highest market volume since last April when turnover hit 6,104 lots.
"It does seem to be mostly switching and all the AAs are in March," the trader said, noting that at least half of the May volume was against the switch.
At 1620 GMT March was up $3.00 at $302.60 after hitting an intraday high of $303.50. May was up $2.80 at $301.00. All other positions were firmer.
March and May open interests have now crossed over as the second-month contract takes up the baton in the little time remaining before the March expiry next week.
Technically, March moved back above the key $300 barrier, following an upward trendline in place since the contract hit a trough of $293.30 in late January.
The position has now pushed through all its short-term moving averages. Momentum indicators have turned higher while remaining in positive territory.
In physical news, Iran's Government Trading Corporation (GTC) tendered to buy 14,000 tonnes of white sugar for April delivery.
Permitted origins are the European Union (excluding the U.K.), Thailand and Brazil.
Paris nearby futures also gained ground although volume was much lighter at 939 lots.
March and May were both up $3.00 at $302.50 and $301.00 respectively.
